tables.name: Table 1
tables.caption: Performance on the validation portion of the Karpathy splits as a function of training metric (2k FC models). Optimizing the CIDEr metric increases the overall performance under the evaluation metrics the most significantly. The performance of the seed cross-entropy (XE) model is also depicted. All models were decoded greedily, with the exception of the (best) XE beam search (BS) result (beam 3).
tables.label: tab:metrics

tables.name: Table 2
tables.caption: Performance of self-critical sequence training (SCST) versus MIXER on the validation portion of the Karpathy splits when trained to optimize the CIDER metric (2k FC models). Using SCST, curriculum learning (CL) is not required. Both signifcantly improve the seed cross-entropy trained model, but SCST significantly outperforms MIXER.

tables.caption: Performance of self-critical sequence training (SCST) versus MIXER and MIXER without a baseline (MIXER-B) on the test portion of the Karpathy splits when trained to optimize the CIDEr metric (FC-2K models). All improve the seed cross-entropy trained model, but SCST outperforms MIXER.
tables.label: rlcompare_table

tables.name: Table 4
tables.caption: Mean/std. performance of SCST versus REINFORCE and REINFORCE with learned baseline (MIXER less CL), for Att2all models (4 seeds) on the Karpathy test set (CIDEr optimized). A one-sample t-test on the gain of SCST over MIXER less CL rejects the null hypothesis on all metrics except ROUGE for (i.e. ).

tables.name: Table 5
tables.caption: Performance on the test portion of the Karpathy splits as a function of training metric ( FC-2K models). Optimizing the CIDEr metric increases the overall performance under the evaluation metrics the most significantly. The performance of the seed cross-entropy (XE) model is also depicted. All models were decoded greedily, with the exception of the XE beam search result, which was optimized to beam 3 on the validation set.
